3.1.1.1.1–6 Section on "Dependent" and Other Terms (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions— Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on a root wholesome state, a root wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root wholesome state, a non-root wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root wholesome state, both root wholesome and non-root wholesome states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a rootless wholesome state, a rootless wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a rootless wholesome state, a rooted wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a rootless wholesome state, both rooted wholesome and rootless wholesome states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome factor that is a root and a wholesome factor that is not a root, a wholesome factor that is a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a wholesome factor that is a root and a wholesome factor that is not a root, a wholesome factor that is not a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a wholesome factor that is a root and a wholesome factor that is not a root, [a wholesome factor that is] both a root and not a root...
Wholesome states arise with root-cause as condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-cause, a wholesome state that is a root-cause arises with object-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu), there are nine; in object condition (ārammaṇa), nine; in predominance condition (adhipati), nine; in proximity condition (anantara), nine; in contiguity condition (samanantara), nine;

in co-nascence condition (sahajāta), nine; in mutuality condition (aññamañña), nine; in dependence condition (nissaya), nine; in strong-dependence condition (upanissaya), nine; in prenascence condition (purejāta), nine; in repetition condition (āsevana), nine;

in kamma condition (kamma), nine; in nutriment condition (āhāra), nine; in faculty condition (indriya), nine; in jhāna condition (jhāna), nine; in path condition (magga), nine; in association condition (sampayutta), nine; in dissociation condition (vippayutta), [nine].
Nine; with presence, nine; with absence, nine; with disappearance, nine; with non-disappearance, nine.
(Positive sequence.
Dependent on a root wholesome state, a root wholesome state arises by way of the not-predominance condition. Root...

Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-cause (*hetu*), both wholesome states that are root-causes and wholesome states that are not root-causes arise by way of the condition of predominance.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not a root-cause, a wholesome state that is not a root-cause arises by way of the condition of predominance... [three].

Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-condition and a wholesome state that is not a root-condition, a wholesome state that is a root-condition arises by way of the not-predominance condition ...
three. Not-precedence, etc.:

Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-condition, a wholesome state that is a root-condition arises by way of the not-precedence condition ... nine; by way of the not-postcedence condition ... nine; by way of the not-repetition condition ... nine.
Dependent on a non-kamma-root wholesome state, a non-root wholesome state arises by way of non-kamma condition.
Dependent on a non-root wholesome state, a non-root wholesome state arises by way of non-kamma condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root and a wholesome state that is not a root, a wholesome state that is not a root arises by way of the not-kamma condition.
[Non-resultant, etc.

With respect to non-predominance: nine; with respect to non-prenascence: nine; with respect to non-postnascence: nine; with respect to non-repetition: nine; with respect to non-kamma: three; with respect to non-resultant: nine;
with respect to non-dissociation: nine. (Negative) With root condition and non-predominance: nine. (Abbreviated;
Positive-Negative) With non-predominance condition and root: nine; with object: nine. (Abbreviated; Negative-Positive)

Chapter of Questions (Pañhāvāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka).
A wholesome state that is a root (hetu) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya), for a wholesome state that is a root.

A wholesome state that is a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state that is not a root. A wholesome state that is a root... [is a condition] for a root... [wholesome state].
A wholesome state that is not a root is related to a wholesome state that is a root by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Object and the rest:
A wholesome state that is a root is related to a wholesome state that is a root by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—three [ways].
A non-root wholesome state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-root wholesome state … three.
Root wholesome and non-root wholesome states are conditions, by way of object-condition, for a root wholesome state … three.
A root wholesome state is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a root wholesome state—predominance as object, co-nascent predominance … three.
A non-root wholesome state is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a non-root wholesome state: object-predominance, co-nascent predominance ... three.

Root wholesome and non-root wholesome states are conditions, by way of predominance condition, for a root wholesome state: object-predominance ... three. [The following applies to] immediate and subsequent conditions, etc.

A wholesome state that is a root is a condition for a wholesome state that is a root by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*), contiguity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*), co-nascence-condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*), mutuality-condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*), and support-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*).

A wholesome state that is a root is a condition for a wholesome state that is a root by way of decisive-support-condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—namely, object-decisive-support, proximity-decisive-support, and natural-decisive-support... [three].

A wholesome state that is not a root (na-hetu) is a condition for a wholesome state that is not a root by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support… three.

Wholesome states that are both roots and not roots are conditions for a wholesome state that is a root by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support… three; they are also conditions by way of repetition condition (āsevana-paccaya)… nine.
A non-root wholesome state is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a non-root wholesome state.
A non-root wholesome state is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a root wholesome state.
A non-root wholesome state is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for both a root wholesome state and a non-root wholesome state.
A wholesome state that is not a root is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a wholesome state that is not a root... three.
A wholesome state that is a root is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a wholesome state that is a root... nine.
A non-root wholesome state is a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for a non-root wholesome state … three.
A root wholesome state is a condition, by way of the path-condition, for a root wholesome state … nine.
Under root: three; under object: nine; under predominance: nine; under proximity: nine; under contiguity: nine; under conascence … [nine].
Nine by mutuality, nine by dependence, nine by strong-dependence, nine by repetition, three by kamma,
three by nutriment, nine by faculty, three by jhāna, nine by path, nine by association, nine by presence, nine by absence,
nine by disappearance, and nine by non-disappearance.
Negative Enumeration (Paccanīyuddhāra):

A wholesome state that is not a root (na-hetu) is a condition for a wholesome state that is not a root by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), by way of conascence-condition (sahajāta-paccaya), and by way of decisive support-condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—three [ways].
A wholesome state that is not a root is a condition for a wholesome state that is not a root by way of object-condition and by way of conascence-condition.

Condition … it is a condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). A wholesome state that is not a root (*na-hetu*) is a condition for a wholesome state that is a root by way of object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*), by way of co-nascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*), and by way of decisive support condition.
A wholesome state that is not a root is a condition for a state that is both a root-possessing wholesome state and a non-root wholesome state by way of object condition.
Condition … by way of conascence-condition … by way of decisive-support-condition.

Wholesome states that are root-conditions and wholesome states that are not root-conditions are conditions for a wholesome state that is a root-condition by way of object-condition, by way of conascence-condition, and by way of decisive-support-condition—three [ways].

In the negative [analysis]: nine in the case of not-root, nine in the case of not-object, nine in the case of not-predominance … pe … nine in the case of not-non-disappearance. (Abbreviated; the negative analysis.)
With root condition, not-object: three … pe … not-absence: three, not-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated; positive-negative.
With not-root condition, object: nine … pe … non-disappearance: nine. (Abbreviated; negative-positive.

3.1.1.2. Unwholesome Section (Akusala-pada) 3.1.1.2.1–6. The Section on Dependence, etc. (Paṭicca-ādi-vāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccaya-catukka)
Root Condition: Dependent on a root unwholesome state, a root unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root unwholesome state, a non-root unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a root unwholesome state...
Dependent on a root that is unwholesome and on a rootless unwholesome state, states that are both roots and unwholesome arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a rootless unwholesome state, a rootless unwholesome state arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a rootless unwholesome state, a state that is both a root and unwholesome arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a rootless unwholesome...
Dependent on a root unwholesome state and non-root unwholesome states, root unwholesome states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root unwholesome state and a non-root unwholesome state, a root unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root unwholesome state and non-root unwholesome states, a non-root unwholesome state arises...
[They] arise by way of root condition. Dependent on a root unwholesome state and a non-root unwholesome state, root unwholesome states and non-root unwholesome states arise by way of root condition.

[There are] nine in the case of the root, nine in the case of the object, nine in the case of the predominance … pe … nine in the case of kamma, nine in the case of nutriment … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance. (Abbreviated; the positive sequence.)
By way of non-root condition: dependent on a non-root unwholesome state, a root unwholesome state arises by way of the non-root condition.
[The same applies to] non-predominance and so forth.
Dependent on a root unwholesome state, a root unwholesome state arises by way of the not-predominance condition … nine … [and so on] … Dependent on a root unwholesome state,
a non-root unwholesome state arises by way of the not-kamma condition.
Dependent on a non-root unwholesome state, a non-root unwholesome state arises by way of the not-kamma condition.
Dependent on a non-root unwholesome state and a root unwholesome state, a non-root unwholesome state arises by way of not-kamma condition. (Abbreviated. In the negative [formula]:
one for not-root, nine for not-predominance, nine for not-prenascence, nine for not-postnascence, nine for not-repetition, three for not-kamma, nine for not-resultant, nine for not-dissociation.
(Negative. With root condition, nine for not-predominance. (Abbreviated; Positive-Negative.)
With not-root condition, there is one [answer] regarding the object. (Abbreviated;
this is the reverse-direct order. (The sections on conascence, conditions, support, association, and conjunction should also be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence. 3.1.1.2.7.

The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root Condition. A root unwholesome state is a condition for a root unwholesome state by way of the root condition. A root unwholesome...
A root (hetu) unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state that is not a root by way of the root-condition (hetupaccaya).

A root unwholesome state is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for both an unwholesome state that is a root and an unwholesome state that is not a root. [The same applies to] the object-condition (ārammaṇa), etc.

A non-causal unwholesome state is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a non-causal unwholesome state ... three.
A non-causal unwholesome state is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a non-causal unwholesome state ... three.
A non-root unwholesome state is a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for a non-root unwholesome state...
three. (Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: nine; under predominance: nine; under proximity: nine; under contiguity:

Three with faculty; three with jhāna; three with path; nine with association; nine with presence; nine with absence;

nine in not-root, nine in not-object, nine in not-predominance, nine in not-proximity, nine in not-contiguity, nine in not-conascence, nine in not-mutuality … pe … nine in not-non-disappearance.

With non-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated; the negative-positive and positive-negative sequences.

Root:
